rationale: Published muscle imaging and clinical characterizations in LGMDR29 (SNUPN-related muscular dystrophy) confirm that axial (paravertebral) and selective distal (peroneal, medial gastrocnemius) degeneration is not restricted to late- or adult-onset disease. In childhood-onset cohorts presenting clinically with proximal limb-girdle weakness, MRI demonstrated predominant fatty infiltration and impairment of the paravertebral, vasti, sartorius, gracilis, peroneal, and medial gastrocnemius muscles. Adult-onset presentations also demonstrate paravertebral, vasti, gastrocnemius, sartorius, and gracilis involvement with overt proximo-distal weakness, demonstrating a conserved topographic selectivity regardless of onset age.

evidence.text: In five patients from two unrelated families presenting with proximal weakness starting in childhood, muscle MRI revealed predominant impairment of paravertebral, vasti, sartorius, gracilis, peroneal, and medial gastrocnemius muscles.

source.title: Biallelic variants in SNUPN cause a limb girdle muscular dystrophy with myofibrillar-like features
source.quote: SNUPN patients show a similar phenotype characterized by proximal weakness starting in childhood, restrictive respiratory dysfunction and prominent contractures... MRI showed predominant impairment of paravertebral, vasti, sartorius, gracilis, peroneal and medial gastrocnemius muscles.

evidence.text: Two adult-onset siblings with novel SNUPN variants presented with proximo-distal and axial weakness with early respiratory involvement, demonstrating involvement in paravertebral, triceps brachii, sartorius, gracilis, vasti, and gastrocnemius muscles.

source.title: SNUPN‐Related Muscular Dystrophy: Novel Phenotypic, Pathological and Functional Protein Insights
source.quote: Two siblings carrying two novel deleterious variants in the SNUPN gene (p.Arg27Cys and p.Cys174Tyr) showed adult-onset proximo-distal and axial muscle weakness with early respiratory involvement... Muscle MRI identified involvement in the paravertebral, triceps brachii, sartorius and gracilis muscles.

new_directions.question_text: Does whole-body Dixon MRI in presymptomatic or very early childhood SNUPN variant carriers reveal subclinical fatty replacement in medial gastrocnemius and paravertebral muscles prior to clinical limb weakness?
new_directions.rationale: Directly testing whether axial and distal involvement precedes proximal weakness will clarify whether the pattern is truly topographically invariant from earliest pathogenesis.

new_directions.question_text: How reliably does the combined MRI pattern of paravertebral, vasti, sartorius, gracilis, and medial gastrocnemius involvement distinguish LGMDR29 from LGMDR1 (calpainopathy) and inclusion body myositis?
new_directions.rationale: Calpainopathy and IBM frequently share hamstring/adductor/quadriceps and distal involvement; evaluating specificity across a broader neuromuscular cohort is essential for differential diagnostic utility.
